newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares end up, medium term outlook bullish.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares end up, medium term outlook bullish.

text.p: Greek equities extended their winning streak to two sessions and analysts said volatility would be the norm heading into the government's policy statements on October 10 but the medium-to-long term outlook was bullish.

"The medium-to-long term market trend is upward but nervousness and volatility will prevail in the short-run as we are nearing the government's policy statements," Emmanuel Varsos, managing director at Investment Analysis, told Reuters.
The September CPI inflation figure will be an important indicator to watch, said Varsos. Greek CPI inflation stood at 8.5 percent year-on-year in August.
"I do not think the September inflation figure will be encouraging," he said.
A National Statistics Service (NSS) official told Reuters that the consumer price inflation will be released on Friday or Monday.
Varsos added that investors should take advantage of market dips and buy selelctive shares.
"Value, quality and growth should be the main determinants of any investment decision," he said.
"I expect blue chips such as the two biggest private banks to perform well after the government's policy statements as domestic and foreign institutionals increase exposure."

Greece's new socialist cabinet was sworn in last week with Yannos Papandoniou elevated to economic "czar", heading both the national economy and finance ministries. The socialists have a comfortable 162-seat majority in the 300-seat parliament.
The Athens general share index closed 0.55 percent, or 5.27 points higher at 965.66 from Tuesday's 960.39 close after opening at 960.76 points.
Turnover stood at 7.39 billion drachmas on volume of 4.13 million shares.
Gainers led decliners 114 to 92 with 36 issues unchanged on 242 traded. Banks gained 1.04 percent, industrials rose 0.52 percent and construction firmed 0.46 percent. Small-caps jumped 1.48 percent.
There was a block trade with 301,740 shares of Athens Medical Centre changing hands at 1,840 drachmas.

The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 558-576 at the close. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, ended down 20 drachmas at 4,075 after light trade.

The recently launched Merrill Lynch stock index call warrant based on a basket of 23 shares was higher at 206.00-216.80 drachmas. It expires on January 9 1998 with a strike price of 1000. It was in the money at 1056.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 4,670-4,951 drachmas at the close. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
